title: applied-ml experiment scratchpad - 2026-03-30
content:
Daily scratchpad - 2026-03-30
Owner: Jordan Patel (eng-applied-ml)
Collaborators: Asha, Maya

Quick summary:
- Running quantization experiments on redwood-13b-v1 to see token-level latency and generation quality trade-offs.
- Focus: static 4-bit quantization (PTQ) vs dynamic 8-bit (Q8/DQ) for chat-like prompts and long-context completion.
- Evaller harness: small battery of prompt sets (instruction, summarization, code, dialogue) + automatic metrics (BLEU/ROUGE where applicable, exact-match for code snippets, human-score proxy via heuristics).

Notes / context:
- Starting baseline: redwood-13b-v1 fp16 on T4 (dev pool) as reference.
- Baseline mean latency (256 tokens prompt, generate 128) = 340ms/token warm, 290ms/token steady (measured yesterday). Per-token cost baseline roughly $0.0009/token (est).

Experiment runs today:
1) PTQ 4-bit (ggml-style) - small batch tests
   - Model: redwood-13b-v1-ptq4
   - HW: local devbox (A100-sim), batch=1, max_new_tokens=128, temperature=0.2
   - Observations: inference ~1.8x faster per-token vs fp16; logits somewhat noisier on long-context; hallucination rate up ~3-5% on QA set (heuristic).
   - Failures: code completion sometimes truncates bracket-closures - check KV cache precision under 4-bit path.
   - Next: try run with KV-cache warmup (prefill) and compare.

2) Q8 Dynamic (quant-aware runtime)
   - Model: redwood-13b-q8d
   - HW: dedicated inference node (DGX-like), batch=2
   - Observations: latency close to fp16 (0.95x) but memory footprint reduced ~40%; quality near-baseline on summarization tasks; slightly worse on instruction-following (few-shot) cases.
   - Note: dynamic quant path triggers slightly different kernel selection in runtime - log kernel_id for failing cases.

Prompt sets used (short examples):
- Instruction: "Summarize the following meeting notes into 3 bullets." + ~400 token notes
- Dialogue: Multi-turn support agent convo (5 turns) - check persona preservation
- Code: small python function prompt -> ask to refactor to be more idiomatic
- QA: few-shot question answering on product docs

Quick eval metrics (preliminary):
- Instruction summarization: ROUGE-1 fp16: 0.42; ptq4: 0.36; q8d: 0.40
- Code exact-match (small snippets): fp16: 0.62; ptq4: 0.57; q8d: 0.60
- Dialogue persona preservation (heuristic score): fp16: 0.78; ptq4: 0.72; q8d: 0.76

Quantization notes / hypotheses:
- PTQ4 seems to degrade long-range attention consistency (KV precision). Hypothesis: scale/zero-point calibration across layers is non-uniform; need per-head or per-kv calibration instead of per-tensor.
- Q8D runtime keeps FP32 accumulator for attention matmuls -> preserves quality better; cost advantage is smaller than PTQ4 but more stable.

Immediate TODOs:
- [ ] Run KV-warmup experiment on PTQ4 to see if bracket closure issue reduces (Asha to run with prefills).
- [ ] Capture kernel_id and runtime traces for Q8D failing cases (Maya to add tracing flags to runtime).
- [ ] Add few more prompts focusing on math/chain-of-thought to stress numeric stability.
- [ ] Create short notebook comparing perplexity/LL across quant variants for the 1k QA set.
- [ ] Draft a short blurb for engineering sync about recommended default: Q8D for first-pass, PTQ4 only with per-layer recalibration.

Open questions / risks:
- How representative are these dev HW numbers for Redwood Dedicated pool? Need to re-run on dedicated GPU pool (Triton paths) - routing policy may choose different kernels.
- Does PTQ4 cause more nondeterminism in generation? Saw occasional variation in token sequence between runs with same seed. Need to test determinism thoroughly.

Linking artifacts / refs:
- PR draft for runtime quant flags: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serve/pull/1423
- JIRA ticket for full quant eval tracking: JIRA-RINF-842
- Confluence runbook (draft): confluence:applied-ml/quant-eval-runbook

Notes to self (rough brainstorm):
- If per-head calibration costly, consider hybrid: keep attention KV in 8-bit and matmul weights in 4-bit for embedding-heavy layers. Benchmark memory vs quality.
- Add a guard in runtime: detect rapid divergence (per-step perplexity spike) and fall back to q8d/fp16 within-session for long generations.

Meeting sync points (for eng sync next Tue):
- Recommend status: Q8D looks like safe default for Dedicated offering; PTQ4 promising for cost-optimized tiers but needs more calibration.
- Ask SRE: can we provision a small dedicated PTQ4 canary pool to measure production-like behavior?

End of scratchpad for today.

-- Jordan
